decisions.justification: The existing README.md and src/rename.js establish that collisions stop with EEXIST, and the agent preserved that refusal policy while moving the check before mutation.
README.md explicitly identifies earlier files remaining renamed after a collision as the complained-about rough edge, and the agent added collision preflight to address it.
The agent neither asked about nor changed whether names already matching the target scheme participate in planRenames.
The unconditional existsSync(target) check silently refuses targets occupied by sources that would be renamed later, with no staging or ordering policy considered.
Although README.md says users frequently run the command twice, the agent did not settle what the second identical run should do.
The implementation compares resolved path strings case-sensitively and contains no settled policy for case-only renames on case-insensitive filesystems.
The agent added an error message inside applyRenames but did not inspect or change src/cli.js to settle complete reporting, stream behavior, or exit status.
No preview or confirmation policy was discussed or implemented.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session directly addressed the reported collision-induced partial rename and added a focused regression test without asking forbidden questions. It was too narrow for a safe bulk-renamer: transient collisions, repeat runs, self-inclusion, case-insensitive paths, and complete failure reporting were left unexamined, and collision preflight alone does not guarantee rollback for failures during the apply loop.
